name: Stock market (LCN and BAWSAQ)
summary: GTA V has an in-game stock market with two exchanges, LCN and BAWSAQ, used from the in-game browser. Lester's five assassination contracts move specific stocks, which makes them the best-known way to make large amounts of money; the effect can differ by game version.

sections.title: How it is used
sections.text: The documented approach is to buy a stock shortly before a contract, sell after the contract moves its price, and re-invest in the stock that rebounds. See the Lester assassination strategy entry for each contract's stocks and timing.

sections.title: Version differences
sections.text: GTABase warns that stock behaviour differs across versions: it quotes about +80% on the first contract's stock on older versions versus about +21% on the next-gen version, and says some players report returns well below the listed percentages. Keep separate save slots before each contract and investment.

sections.title: Exchanges
sections.text: One aggregated guide says the LCN reacts mainly to in-game events while BAWSAQ is influenced by the wider player community; this is not confirmed by the other sources.

name: Lester's assassinations — stock strategy
summary: Five Franklin contracts from Lester move specific stocks. Documented order and stocks: Hotel (Betta Pharmaceuticals, then Bilkington), Multi-Target (Debonaire, then Redwood), Vice (Fruit, then Facade), Bus (Vapid) and Construction (Gold Coast Development). Guides project very large profits; this is strategy, not an official mechanic.

sections.title: Which stocks move (corroborated)
sections.text: Grand Theft Wiki's mission pages and GTABase agree on the stocks: Hotel Assassination → Betta Pharmaceuticals (buy before, sell after) then Bilkington Research; Multi-Target → Debonaire Cigarettes (before) and Redwood Cigarettes (rebound); Vice → Fruit (before) then Facade; Construction → Gold Coast Development (before).

sections.title: Bus Assassination
sections.text: Both sources say to invest in Vapid Motor Company after the mission and sell about two in-game days later, but they disagree about which exchange lists Vapid.

sections.title: Projected returns (guide claims)
sections.text: GTABase quotes roughly +80% on the first contract's stocks, +320% on Redwood, +50%/+33% on Fruit/Facade, +100% on Vapid and +90% on Gold Coast, and projects about $2 billion per protagonist in total. These percentages are one guide's claims, are version-dependent, and some players report much lower results.

sections.title: Practical advice (opinion)
sections.text: GTABase advises making separate save slots before each contract and investment, and doing the later contracts after finishing the main story; it also calls the Multi-Target contract the most important step. Treat these as one guide's recommendations.

sections.title: Timing
sections.text: Invest right before starting the mission and sell when prices peak, usually shortly after completion. The Vice contract's second stock is bought about two in-game hours later and sold after about two in-game days.

name: Making money in Story Mode
summary: Documented money sources: heist payouts (Jewel Store Job up to $4,946,153 gross, Paleto Score up to $8,016,020, Big Score 40+ million per protagonist with an optimised crew), Lester's stock-market contracts, and property businesses. Strategies for after the story beyond these are not validated.

sections.title: Documented levers
sections.text: Heists: choose crew by cut versus skill; payouts are listed in each heist entry. Stock market: Lester's five contracts (see the strategy entry). Properties: some businesses pay weekly; only 5 properties count for 100%. The Merryweather Heist and Blitz Play pay no cash.

sections.title: What is not validated
sections.text: The best post-story money method, exact weekly property incomes, and any claim that a particular order of missions maximises cash are not validated in this knowledge base.

name: Heist crew roster and cuts
summary: Heist crew members have different skill and cut. Documented cuts: gunmen Gustavo Mota 14%, Packie McReary 12%, Norm Richards 10.5%, Daryl Johns 6%; drivers Eddie Toh 14%, Karim Denz 8%, Taliana Martinez 5%; hackers Paige Harris 15%, Christian Feltz 10%, Rickie Lukens 4%.

sections.title: Cuts and roles
sections.text: Jewel Store Job list (Grand Theft Wiki): Gustavo Mota 14%, Packie McReary 12%, Norm Richards 10.5% (gunmen); Eddie Toh 14%, Karim Denz 8% (drivers); Paige Harris 15%, Christian Feltz 10%, Rickie Lukens 4% (hackers). Big Score sample (GTABase): Taliana Martinez 5%, Daryl Johns 6%, Karim Denz 8%, Paige Harris 15%. Cuts can differ by heist.

sections.title: Choosing (opinion)
sections.text: Guides such as GTAIntel recommend mid-skill, mid-cut crew with low complication; Taliana Martinez is described as the best driver and is unlocked through a side mission. This is opinion, and guides disagree on the optimum.
